sources.title: Kyushu National Museum: The Ashikaga Shoguns
sources.note: Official exhibition, chapters 1, 2 and 4, read directly. 1336 administration, Yoshimitsu political consolidation, weakening authority and Yoshiaki expelled in 1573. Avoid source slip claiming Takauji sent ships to Ming: he died before that dynasty began.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: Muromachi Period (1392 to 1573)
sources.note: Department of Asian Art essay, October 2002. Indexed official full text read. Broad provincial power, Onin War 1467 to 1477, commerce and cultural patronage. Museum uses narrower art-period dating than the indexed political record.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: Japan, 1000 to 1400, chronology
sources.note: Official chronology indexed text, events 1333, 1336 and 1338; rival courts until 1392. Different authored timeline from general Muromachi essay.

sources.title: Kyoto National Museum: Licenses for Trade between Japan and Ming China
sources.note: Mamoru Shimosaka, translated by Melissa Rinne, 1993. Direct read. Yoshimitsu 1401 embassy; copper coins/silk thread imports, sulfur/swords/fans exports; matching half-character licenses. Avoid overbroad statement that no private trade occurred before 1401.

sources.title: Ichijodani Asakura Family Site Museum: archaeological site walk
sources.note: Direct Japanese text read, sections 14 bead making, 16 doctor, 17 houses and 21 Nanyo-ji poem. Indexed same-page text also describes typical six-metre-frontage house with well and rear toilet; other houses lack private facilities. Public poem fragment 糸ざくら occurs in Yoshiaki poem of spring 1568, reproduced by museum; reading ito-zakura and translation weeping cherry supplied. No autograph claim.

sources.title: Ichijodani Asakura Family Site Museum: excavation and history
sources.note: Official excavating museum, direct read. Castle town burned by Nobunaga forces in 1573, excavation since 1967, over 1.7 million excavated materials at time of source. Used for discovery and regional destruction, not for claim all medieval cities vanished.

sources.title: Hiroshima Prefectural Museum of History: Recreating Kusado Sengen
sources.note: Direct Japanese text. Fourteenth-century town reconstruction distinguishes excavated plans/objects from interpretive staged families and activities. Sections townhouses and market/docks; public paragraphs explicitly call it a museum reconstruction. Shared wells and work/living floors belong to reconstruction grounded in excavation and comparative images.

sources.title: National Museum of Japanese History: Gender in Japanese History (2020)
sources.note: Indexed original exhibition text checked, including Politics and Gender in Medieval Japan; direct fetch timed out. Search metadata mislabels page Konbu and Miyok, but body is the 2020 Gender exhibition. Nyobo hosho became frequent official documents in Muromachi/Sengoku.

sources.title: Asian Art Museum: Muromachi Period Tea
sources.note: Direct read. Shoin gatherings, curatorial service, Murata Shuko and merchant hosts; keep later Rikyu developments beyond 1573 outside this card.

sources.title: Tokyo National Museum e-Museum: Landscape with ink broken, Sesshu (1495)
sources.note: Full indexed original English and Japanese museum record read; simplified URL fetch failed. A-282, ink on paper, 1495, inscription describing student Josui Soen and six Kyoto monks; training in China and Japan. No direct inscription transcription asserted.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: Seto tea jar, circa 1500
sources.note: Official object record, full indexed original read. 29.100.650, clay and thick brown glaze, height 8.3 cm. Date approximate; no claim of universal ownership.

sources.title: Agency for Cultural Affairs: Keitekishu autograph manuscript
sources.note: Government cultural-property record, direct read. Manase Dosan, eight-volume autograph work presented to emperor in 1574, based on more than thirty years of treatment records. Explicitly later than card end, but evidence for preceding decades of practice. No efficacy claims.

proposedOverrides.name: Muromachi

fell.text: Oda Nobunaga expelled Ashikaga Yoshiaki from Kyoto in 1573.

proposedOverrides.summary: Ashikaga warrior government, provincial power and a flourishing world of medieval Japanese trade and culture.

batchIdentityNotes.related: Indexed alias Ashikaga shogunate is the same government. No shared card association with japan (1492 to 1530) or japan-warring-states (1530 to 1650); their different intervals and outlines need separate review.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: Opening exposes geometry/index mismatch. Broad outline is not proof of equal shogunal control. Museum art histories sometimes date Muromachi from 1392; political narrative includes preceding rival courts. Regional Ichijodani and Kusado examples explicitly named.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Museum-transmitted Yoshiaki poem of 1568; short Japanese noun 糸ざくら, ito-zakura, weeping cherry; no contemporary-autograph verification claimed.
